ukmt-tmc-2017-regional-shuttle-02.title: Solution
ukmt-tmc-2017-regional-shuttle-02.body:
The angles total $360$: $7(11)+8(11)+9(11)=264$, so $12K=96$ and $K=8$.

**Answer: 8**

Here $T=11$ comes from the previous question of the chain.

ukmt-tmc-2017-regional-shuttle-03.title: Solution
ukmt-tmc-2017-regional-shuttle-03.body:
There are $7$ pieces of mean length 22 cm, so $154$ cm is cut. The rope is $274$ cm, so $K=274-154=120$.

**Answer: 120**

Here $T=8$ comes from the previous question of the chain.

ukmt-tmc-2017-regional-shuttle-04.title: Solution
ukmt-tmc-2017-regional-shuttle-04.body:
Triangle $ABD$ has area $\frac12\times30\times120=1800$. So triangle $ADC$ has area $6000-1800=4200$.

**Answer: 4200**

Here $T=120$ comes from the previous question of the chain.

ukmt-tmc-2017-regional-shuttle-06.title: Solution
ukmt-tmc-2017-regional-shuttle-06.body:
The repeating block has 16 digits: $1,7,6,4,7,0,5,8,8,2,3,5,2,9,4,1$. The $(2017+6)=2023$rd decimal place is the same as place $2023-16\times126=7$ in the block (since $16\times126=2016$), and the 7th digit is $5$.

**Answer: 5**

Here $T=6$ comes from the previous question of the chain.

ukmt-tmc-2017-regional-shuttle-07.title: Solution
ukmt-tmc-2017-regional-shuttle-07.body:
$20T=100$ and $32T=160$. $100=2^2\cdot5^2$, $160=2^5\cdot5$, so the LCM is $2^5\cdot5^2=800$.

**Answer: 800**

Here $T=5$ comes from the previous question of the chain.

ukmt-tmc-2017-regional-shuttle-08.title: Solution
ukmt-tmc-2017-regional-shuttle-08.body:
Let the short diagonal be $d$. Area $=\frac12\cdot d\cdot4d=2d^2=800$, so $d^2=400$ and $d=20$.

**Answer: 20**

Here $T=800$ comes from the previous question of the chain.

ukmt-tmc-2017-regional-shuttle-09.title: Solution
ukmt-tmc-2017-regional-shuttle-09.body:
The product in brackets is $\frac1{120}$, so $K=1\div\frac1{120}=120$.

**Answer: 120**

ukmt-tmc-2017-regional-shuttle-10.title: Solution
ukmt-tmc-2017-regional-shuttle-10.body:
Let $\angle BCD=\theta$. In triangle $BCD$: $120+2\theta+\theta=180$, so $\theta=20$. Then $\angle BDA=60^\circ$. Angle $ABD=180-120=60^\circ$ (straight line $ABC$). In triangle $ABD$, $x=180-60-60=60$.

**Answer: 60**

Here $T=120$ comes from the previous question of the chain.

ukmt-tmc-2017-regional-shuttle-11.title: Solution
ukmt-tmc-2017-regional-shuttle-11.body:
Here $T-12=48$. Let rectangle $EFGH$ have length $\ell$ and width $2\ell$; then $ABCD$ has width $6\ell$ and length $3\ell$. The shaded region is $ABCD$ with $EFGH$ cut out, so its perimeter is $2(3\ell+6\ell)+2(\ell+2\ell)=24\ell=48$, so $\ell=2$. Area $=3\ell\cdot6\ell-\ell\cdot2\ell=18\ell^2-2\ell^2=16\ell^2=64$.

**Answer: 64**

Here $T=60$ comes from the previous question of the chain.

ukmt-tmc-2017-regional-shuttle-12.title: Solution
ukmt-tmc-2017-regional-shuttle-12.body:
Expand: LHS $=\frac x8+\frac T{32}-\frac x{32}-\frac T{128}=\frac{3x}{32}+\frac{3T}{128}$; RHS $=\frac x8+\frac T{64}$. So $\frac{3x}{32}-\frac{4x}{32}=\frac T{64}-\frac{3T}{128}$, i.e. $-\frac x{32}=-\frac T{128}$ and $x=\frac T4=16$.

**Answer: 16**

Here $T=64$ comes from the previous question of the chain.

ukmt-tmc-2017-regional-shuttle-14.title: Solution
ukmt-tmc-2017-regional-shuttle-14.body:
The interior angles of a hexagon total $720^\circ$. $17+20+17+18+16=88$, so $88T+kT=720$. With $T=8$: $704+8k=720$, $k=2$.

**Answer: 2**

Here $T=8$ comes from the previous question of the chain.

ukmt-tmc-2017-regional-shuttle-15.title: Solution
ukmt-tmc-2017-regional-shuttle-15.body:
$T$ thousand men $=2000$. Each stage leaves 80%: $2000\times0.8^3=2000\times0.512=1024$.

**Answer: 1024**

Here $T=2$ comes from the previous question of the chain.

ukmt-tmc-2017-regional-shuttle-16.title: Solution
ukmt-tmc-2017-regional-shuttle-16.body:
With $T=1024$: the mean is $512$ so the total is $2560$; the mode is $768$ and the range is $512$. Write the numbers in order $a\le b\le c\le d\le e$ with $e=a+512$. The mode $768$ must appear at least twice, and no other value may appear twice.

If the median $c$ were $768$ or more, then at least three numbers would be at least $768$ and $e\ge768$ gives $a\ge256$, so the total would be at least $256+256+768\times3=2816>2560$. So $c<768$ and the two $768$s are $d$ and $e$. Then $a=768-512=256$ and $b+c=2560-256-1536=768$. We need $b\ne256$ (otherwise 256 would also occur twice), so $b\ge257$ and $c\le511$. The set $256,257,511,768,768$ works, so the largest possible median is $511$.

**Answer: 511**

Here $T=1024$ comes from the previous question of the chain.
